items.title: Wall Street futures surge toward best week in months on Nvidia lifeline
items.take: Wall Street reopened for its shortened Black Friday session with a strong bid: Nasdaq-100 futures jumped about 2% pre-market as beaten-down chip and AI names (Nvidia, Sandisk, Micron, AMD, Oracle, CoreWeave) bounced back. After Wednesday's late recovery, the tape is on course for its best week in months.

items.title: Dow futures surge 650 points: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens
items.take: Analysts caution the rebound is technical buying, not a verdict on the AI-spend-and-returns questions that drove November's selloff, and thin holiday volumes can magnify moves either way. December brings inflation prints, jobs data and a Fed meeting to settle it.

items.title: Adobe forecasts record $12.9 billion online for Black Friday
items.take: Adobe projects $12.9 billion in US online sales today, up 9.2%, on the way to a record $275.1 billion season, with $82.5 billion already spent online this month. The catch: the NRF expects 182.7 million shoppers, down from 202.9 million, and much of the growth is price, not volume (PwC puts real growth near 2.8%).

items.title: U.S. proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU
items.take: The new Section 301 overcapacity levies land on China (an added 20%, about 45% total), the EU, Japan, India and ten more economies, with hearings set for January 25. Investors spent the holiday weighing whether this week's bounce survives full volumes and the tariff overhang next week.

items.title: Thanksgiving storm pounds US East Coast, Macy's parade postponed to Saturday
items.take: A nor'easter flooded the East Coast on Thanksgiving, canceling roughly 400 flights and prompting a New Jersey state of emergency, and Macy's moved its 100th-anniversary parade to Saturday for the first time ever. The weather is a real drag on holiday travel and foot traffic just as the biggest shopping weekend starts.
